correctness.rationale: Exact expected depth generating function and Gaussian tilt yield independent Bernoulli count K and iid N(1,1) marks under an exact many-to-one identity. Concentration of K, bounded marked empirical means, quadratic energy and uniform centered partial sums is exponentially sharp. For any defect with rate a>0, n^{-(sqrt(e)-epsilon)} times the tilted first moment is O(n^{epsilon-a}); take epsilon<a and use the genuinely published maximum lower bound. This excludes every anomalous near-peak path, proving all asserted maximizer properties. All finite checker identities passed; the finite checks are not taken as infinite proof.

The result distinguishes typical N(0,1) marks from N(1,1) extreme-path marks, quantifies both negative-step density and energy, and applies to an intrinsic observable of a recently studied random-tree GFF rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
